user.title: Connect to Hearth
user.description: Paste the pairing token from your Hearth dashboard. The integration will open an outbound connection to Hearth; no ports need to be forwarded.

error.invalid_url: The Hearth URL must start with https://
error.rate_limited: Too many attempts. Wait a minute and try again.
error.cannot_connect: Could not reach Hearth. Check the URL and your internet connection.

abort.already_configured: This Hearth installation is already configured.

connection.title: Connection to Hearth
connection.description: Installation {installation_id} at {hub_url} is currently {status}. Turning the connection off closes the outbound link immediately; nothing can reach this Home Assistant until you turn it back on. The connection switch entity does the same.

capabilities.title: What the AI may access
capabilities.description: Each switch grants the AI (your own AI client through the Hearth connector, and the Managed assistant) one area. Reads never change anything. Writes create, edit, and delete items the same way the Home Assistant editor does. The last two let it act on your home immediately and are off until you turn them on. On top of all of this, only entities exposed to Assist (Settings → Voice assistants → Expose) are ever visible, and locks, alarms, cameras, and location entities are never accessible.

data.cap_services_read: Read the service catalog (for authoring actions)
data.cap_devices_control: Control devices now (lights, switches, climate, covers, media, and so on)
data.cap_routines_run: Activate scenes and run scripts you already created

data_description.cap_devices_control: Lets it act on your home as you speak, for example "turn on the kitchen lights". Locks, alarms, and cameras stay blocked.
data_description.cap_routines_run: A script does whatever you wrote in it, which may include actions Hearth itself is not allowed to perform. Enable this only if you trust your own scripts.
